reason: The hose and pump are the only offered combination, and they seem useful for moving recovered water to the garden.
expectation: I expect to make a pumped water line, though it may still need connecting to the garden port.

effect: The hose and pump form a return loop that splashes water above the reservoirs before sending it back to the beds. It still appears to need a connection at the garden port.
reaction: The splash is a useful detail, though I am curious how the loop connects to the dehumidifier outlet.
reason: Connecting the loop to the garden service port is the only offered combination and seems like the next step toward returning moisture to the roots.
expectation: I expect the loop to be installed at the garden port and to route recovered water to the beds, though the connection details are uncertain.

effect: The service port connects treated condensate through a nutrient doser to the reservoir, while both beds drain back through the aerating loop. That resolves how recovered moisture reaches the garden.
reaction: I appreciated the connection detail; it answered my question about the dehumidifier outlet.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the loop was most worthwhile because it showed how treated condensate and nutrient dosing fit into the garden's water cycle.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the loop was less engaging as a decision because it was the only offered combination, though the splash detail was useful.

surprise.text: I was curious to learn that the return splashes above the reservoir and that condensate enters through a nutrient doser.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary, although both were the only offered combinations.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the completed water cycle made me curious about how the other systems will develop, even though this chapter offered little choice.
